'''Lussekatter''' or '''luciabullar''' are Scandinavian saffron buns served on [[w:St. Lucia Day|St. Lucia Day]] (13 December).

==Ingredients==

*2 packages (4½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]]) active dry [[Cookbook:yeast|yeast]]
*¼ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] lukewarm water
*½ tsp crushed (¼ tsp powdered) [[Cookbook:saffron|saffron]] threads
*¾ cup (180 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Half and Half|half and half]], lukewarm
*½ cup (120 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]]) melted [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]], beaten
*¾ cup (180 g) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
*4–5 cups sifted [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
*[[Cookbook:Raisin|Raisins]] to decorate

==Procedure==
#Combine the yeast and warm water.
#Mix saffron into the warm half and half and let stand.
#Combine the yeast and saffron mixtures. Mix in the melted butter, eggs, sugar, and salt.
#Mix half of flour into the wet mixture and beat until well-blended.
#Mix in additional flour until [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] is smooth but not too firm. [[Cookbook:Kneading|Knead]] on floured surface for ten minutes.
#Place dough in buttered bowl and let rise about 1½ hours or until doubled in volume.
#Divide the dough into multiple pieces. Roll each piece into a 7 inch-long snake, and form into an 'S' shape with the ends curled in. Place a raisin in each curl.
#Place buns on buttered [[Cookbook:Baking Sheet|sheet pan]], cover, and let rise 45 minutes. 
#[[Cookbook:Brush|Brush]] with beaten egg and [[Cookbook:Baking|bake]] at 375–400°F (190–200°C) for 10–15 minutes until golden and cooked through.
